threads.body: Wording here is internally inconsistent: “native instrumentation” (per the linked OTel glossary) implies using the OpenTelemetry API, but the examples that follow describe telemetry/instrumentation that is *not* based on the OTel API. Reword to avoid implying that “native instrumentation” can be non-OTel.
threads.hunk:
@@ -144,6 +144,56 @@ you start one of these tasks:
 
 Please contribute back anything you learn while using the skills that could help improve them!
 
+## When to add an instrumentation here
+
+We encourage libraries to emit GenAI telemetry themselves, following the
+[GenAI semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai),
+either with [native instrumentation](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/glossary/#natively-instrumented)
+(using the OpenTelemetry API directly) or through a plugin maintained by the
+same authors. Telemetry is best owned and maintained closest to the library it
+describes; re-instrumenting such a library here duplicates ownership and
+fragments the ecosystem.
+
+Some existing native instrumentations are not compatible with OpenTelemetry — for
+example, they may use tracing primitives not based on the OpenTelemetry API,
+export via OTLP only without interacting with OpenTelemetry context and SDK
+configuration, or not follow the GenAI semantic conventions.

threads.body: This heuristic is likely too strong: a dependency on `opentelemetry-api` can also mean context propagation helpers or optional integration points, not necessarily that the library “ships native instrumentation”. Tightening the wording will reduce false positives while keeping the intent.

+## Before adding a new instrumentation
+
+Before scaffolding a new instrumentation package, check whether the target library already
+provides its own GenAI telemetry, and get the user's acknowledgement before proceeding. Follow the
+[When to add an instrumentation here](CONTRIBUTING.md#when-to-add-an-instrumentation-here) policy.
+
+- **Check the library's dependencies.** A dependency on `opentelemetry-api` (or other
+  `opentelemetry-*` packages) in the library's metadata (`pyproject.toml` / `setup.py` /
+  `setup.cfg` / lockfile) usually means it ships native instrumentation — research it before
+  writing any code.

threads.body: This guidance would be more accurate if it distinguished runtime deps from dev/test deps: many repos include `opentelemetry-*` as development dependencies for examples/tests without shipping native instrumentation. Consider clarifying “runtime dependency” / “install requirements” to reduce noise for reviewers.

threads.body:
"natively instrumented or has a first-party plugin" already implies the OpenTelemetry API (that's the glossary definition linked in the callout), but the first bullet right below branches on it *not* being based on the OTel API. Suggest splitting the two questions so the bullets and the flowchart line up:

```suggestion
Before adding a new instrumentation, check whether the target library already
emits first-party GenAI telemetry (built in, or through a first-party plugin),
whether it's based on the OpenTelemetry API, and how closely it follows the
GenAI semantic conventions:
```
